svg.title: Why a Pod stays Pending: the scheduler filters nodes
svg.desc: The scheduler starts with all nodes and removes the ones that cannot take the Pod: not enough CPU or memory (K01), a taint the Pod does not tolerate (K16), a nodeSelector or node affinity that does not match (K17), or anti-affinity with another Pod (K18). If none are left the Pod stays Pending and the Events explain why.

svg.text: The scheduler removes every node that cannot take the Pod; when none are left, it waits

svg.text: Pending is not an error. It is the scheduler saying: I looked at every node and none qualifies.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

svg.text: kubectl describe pod → Events: 0/3 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint(s), 2 Insufficient memory.

svg.text: The Events line names the exact filter that said no.
